patient_display_policy: Numerical trial outcomes and study-population counts are excluded from patient content. Use service-facts.patient_updates.evidence instead.

mechanisms.00254: Nonsteroidal, reversible aromatase inhibitor; reduces peripheral conversion of androgens to oestrogens. It is not an ovarian-suppression drug or an ER degrader.
mechanisms.00371: Nonsteroidal, reversible aromatase inhibitor; oestrogen deprivation rather than ER antagonism or ovarian suppression.
mechanisms.00376: Steroidal, irreversible aromatase inactivator. It mimics an androgen substrate and inactivates the enzyme; it does not degrade the oestrogen receptor. This mechanism does not establish superiority or interchangeable sequencing with nonsteroidal AIs.

evidence_records.trial_acronym: ATAC: ten-year analysis of initial adjuvant anastrozole versus tamoxifen
evidence_records.publication_title: ATAC: ten-year analysis of initial adjuvant anastrozole versus tamoxifen
evidence_records.study_design: Postmenopausal early breast cancer; 6,241 women in the two monotherapy groups, including 5,216 with hormone-receptor-positive disease; median follow-up 120 months.
evidence_records.trial_population: Postmenopausal early breast cancer; 6,241 women in the two monotherapy groups, including 5,216 with hormone-receptor-positive disease; median follow-up 120 months.
evidence_records.evidence_context: Initial adjuvant treatment; not a metastatic or neoadjuvant benefit estimate.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Disease-free survival; recurrence endpoints and overall mortality also reported.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: In the HR-positive subgroup, DFS HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.78–0.95) and time-to-recurrence HR 0.79 (0.70–0.89) favoured anastrozole. Absolute recurrence difference at 10 years was 4.3 percentage points. Overall mortality was not significantly different: HR 0.95 (0.84–1.06).
key_findings: In the HR-positive subgroup, DFS HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.78–0.95) and time-to-recurrence HR 0.79 (0.70–0.89) favoured anastrozole.
Absolute recurrence difference at 10 years was 4.3 percentage points. Overall mortality was not significantly different: HR 0.95 (0.84–1.06).
evidence_records.limitations: Adjuvant results cannot supply an advanced-disease prognosis or authorise AI monotherapy with functioning ovaries. Fractures were more frequent during active anastrozole treatment. The trial is not evidence for restarting a complete five-year course after a tamoxifen switch.
evidence_records.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical and oncology pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.trial_acronym: BIG 1-98: long-term follow-up of letrozole versus tamoxifen
evidence_records.publication_title: BIG 1-98: long-term follow-up of letrozole versus tamoxifen
evidence_records.study_design: Postmenopausal HR-positive early breast cancer; 8,010 randomized overall, including a 4,922-patient monotherapy comparison. Long-term follow-up was available from participating centres for 3,833 of 4,433 eligible patients; median follow-up 12.6 years.
evidence_records.trial_population: Postmenopausal HR-positive early breast cancer; 8,010 randomized overall, including a 4,922-patient monotherapy comparison. Long-term follow-up was available from participating centres for 3,833 of 4,433 eligible patients; median follow-up 12.6 years.
evidence_records.evidence_context: Initial adjuvant treatment; latest long-term primary report identified in this audit.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Disease-free survival; other efficacy and safety endpoints also followed.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: At median 12.6 years, the DFS estimate for letrozole versus tamoxifen was HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.81–1.01); this confidence interval includes no difference. The latest report therefore must not be described as a statistically significant long-term DFS advantage on the strength of the earlier 8.7-year estimate.
key_findings: At median 12.6 years, the DFS estimate for letrozole versus tamoxifen was HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.81–1.01); this confidence interval includes no difference.
The latest report therefore must not be described as a statistically significant long-term DFS advantage on the strength of the earlier 8.7-year estimate.
evidence_records.limitations: The randomized trial was extended observationally after sponsor follow-up; weighted analyses addressed participating-centre coverage. Attrition and selective crossover complicate interpretation. Earlier significant estimates and this later estimate are different timepoints/analyses, not interchangeable numbers. This adjuvant trial does not quantify benefit in neoadjuvant or advanced disease.
evidence_records.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical and oncology pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.trial_acronym: MA.17: extended adjuvant letrozole following tamoxifen
evidence_records.publication_title: MA.17: extended adjuvant letrozole following tamoxifen
evidence_records.study_design: 5,187 postmenopausal women after approximately 5 years of tamoxifen; double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial, median follow-up 30 months at this updated report.
evidence_records.trial_population: 5,187 postmenopausal women after approximately 5 years of tamoxifen; double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial, median follow-up 30 months at this updated report.
evidence_records.intervention: Letrozole 2.5 mg daily, planned for 5 years
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Disease-free survival; distant disease-free survival and overall survival secondary.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: DFS HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.45–0.76; P<0.001) and distant DFS HR 0.60 (0.43–0.84; P=0.002) favoured letrozole. Overall survival was not significantly improved across the whole randomized population: HR 0.82 (0.57–1.19; P=0.30).
key_findings: DFS HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.45–0.76; P<0.001) and distant DFS HR 0.60 (0.43–0.84; P=0.002) favoured letrozole.
Overall survival was not significantly improved across the whole randomized population: HR 0.82 (0.57–1.19; P=0.30).
evidence_records.limitations: Stopped early for benefit, which affects follow-up and later crossover interpretation. The node-positive OS subgroup finding must not be presented as a whole-trial survival benefit. Supports a defined post-tamoxifen extension, not indefinite therapy or automatic extension after every preceding AI course.
evidence_records.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical and oncology pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.study_design: 337 postmenopausal women with untreated ER- and/or PgR-positive primary breast cancer initially unsuitable for breast-conserving surgery; randomized double-blind comparison.
evidence_records.trial_population: 337 postmenopausal women with untreated ER- and/or PgR-positive primary breast cancer initially unsuitable for breast-conserving surgery; randomized double-blind comparison.
evidence_records.evidence_context: Neoadjuvant treatment, distinct from adjuvant recurrence prevention and advanced-disease control.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Objective clinical response assessed by palpation.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Clinical response was 55% versus 36% (P<0.001), favouring letrozole. Breast-conserving surgery occurred in 45% versus 35% (P=0.022).
key_findings: Clinical response was 55% versus 36% (P<0.001), favouring letrozole.
evidence_records.limitations: Response and surgical conversion are not overall-survival outcomes. The historical study population is not identical to current labelled neoadjuvant selection. Its four-month duration must not replace NCCP’s response-guided 4–8-month pathway or justify delaying indicated surgery.
evidence_records.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical and oncology pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.trial_acronym: IES: long-term follow-up after switching from tamoxifen to exemestane
evidence_records.publication_title: IES: long-term follow-up after switching from tamoxifen to exemestane
evidence_records.study_design: 4,724 postmenopausal women who remained disease-free after 2–3 years of adjuvant tamoxifen; ER-positive/unknown analysis comprised 4,599; median follow-up 120 months.
evidence_records.trial_population: 4,724 postmenopausal women who remained disease-free after 2–3 years of adjuvant tamoxifen; ER-positive/unknown analysis comprised 4,599; median follow-up 120 months.
evidence_records.intervention: Switch to exemestane 25 mg daily to complete 5 total years of endocrine therapy
evidence_records.comparator: Continue tamoxifen to complete 5 total years
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Breast-cancer-free survival (BCFS), censoring intercurrent deaths, was the principal long-term survival endpoint of interest.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: In ER-positive/unknown disease, 10-year BCFS absolute difference was 4.0 percentage points (95% CI 1.2–6.7); HR 0.81 (0.72–0.92), favouring the switch. Overall survival in that analysis was not statistically significant: HR 0.89 (0.78–1.01; P=0.08), absolute difference 2.1 percentage points (−0.5 to 4.6).
key_findings: In ER-positive/unknown disease, 10-year BCFS absolute difference was 4.0 percentage points (95% CI 1.2–6.7); HR 0.81 (0.72–0.92), favouring the switch.
Overall survival in that analysis was not statistically significant: HR 0.89 (0.78–1.01; P=0.08), absolute difference 2.1 percentage points (−0.5 to 4.6).
evidence_records.limitations: BCFS is not interchangeable with DFS or overall survival. This strategy totals five endocrine-treatment years; it does not add five exemestane years to the preceding tamoxifen course. It cannot establish benefit for every broader NCCP extended-adjuvant indication, premenopausal monotherapy or advanced-disease prognosis.
evidence_records.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical and oncology pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.trial_acronym: Exemestane versus megestrol after tamoxifen failure in advanced breast cancer
evidence_records.publication_title: Exemestane versus megestrol after tamoxifen failure in advanced breast cancer
evidence_records.study_design: 769 postmenopausal women with advanced breast cancer progressing after tamoxifen; randomized double-blind trial: exemestane 366, megestrol 403.
evidence_records.trial_population: 769 postmenopausal women with advanced breast cancer progressing after tamoxifen; randomized double-blind trial: exemestane 366, megestrol 403.
evidence_records.comparator: Megestrol acetate 40 mg four times daily (160 mg total daily)
evidence_records.evidence_context: Advanced disease after tamoxifen failure, not an adjuvant trial.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Objective response and time-to-event efficacy outcomes in advanced disease.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Median time to progression was 20.3 versus 16.6 weeks (P=0.037), favouring exemestane. Overall response was 15.0% versus 12.4%; this difference should not be labelled statistically significant.
key_findings: Median time to progression was 20.3 versus 16.6 weeks (P=0.037), favouring exemestane.
Overall response was 15.0% versus 12.4%; this difference should not be labelled statistically significant.
evidence_records.limitations: Historical post-tamoxifen population and comparator predate modern CDK4/6, PI3K/AKT and oral SERD treatment sequences. Do not use these short historical medians as an individual prognosis or as expected benefit following current targeted combinations. Keep this advanced evidence separate from IES adjuvant BCFS.
evidence_records.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical and oncology pharmacy review pending

coverage_limitations: Selected regimen-relevant primary reports, including later follow-up, were reviewed; this is not a systematic treatment-sequencing review.
Anastrozole and letrozole advanced disease do not receive a manufactured benefit estimate from adjuvant data.
No study establishes ovarian suppression from an AI tablet alone or interchangeable dose/monitoring rules across the three drugs.
